newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher, central bank intervenes.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher, central bank intervenes.

text.p: The won closed higher versus the U.S. currency on Tuesday in line with the yen's strength against the dollar in world markets but dealers said central bank intervention had limited the won's rise.

They said the Bank of Korea began buying dollars when the won rose to a high of 890.00, spurred by the dollar's fall in Tokyo. The dollar fell as low as 111.98 yen, its lowest since December 6, 1996, due to expectations that the interest rate gap between the United States and Japan would narrow.
The won finished at 890.60, compared to Monday's close of 891.20.
After opening at 890.70, it fell to 891.50 on dollar short-covering after the Bank of Korea stepped in.
The central bank never confirms its intervention.

Dealers were divided over the future won/dollar movement. "I cannot rule out the possibility for the won to surge to the 800 level, given the Korean economy's dependence on the Japanese currency," said a dealer.
But another dealer said the current yen/dollar fluctuation was very unstable.
Wednesday's mid-rate is expected to be fixed at 890.60 against 891.30 today.
